mustFix.title: The entry's premise misreads D-056's pinned subject, and the ineligible half of the same paragraph is left with no stated standing
mustFix.finding: The draft's reason for existing is that 'D-056 then named the eligible-in-kind set by identity ... The closed name list cannot admit a row created after D-056', and it supersedes that list as the definition of eligibility. Measured against D-056's own pinned turn-2 subject (docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-056.turn2.draft.md, dfb0c2af..., mode 0444, the exact file the COORD entry pins as its adopted subject), that reading is not what D-056 decided. The subject already states eligibility AS A PROPERTY at its Eligibility heading — 'A later SATISFIED re-record of a slice-affecting architecture row may use this amendment only when all of the following are true of that row at the moment of that later cycle' — and it labels the four-row table 'Motivating later candidates (not performed here)', not a definition. Its ineligible table is headed 'Ineligible today (named, not exhaustive)' and its body reads 'not eligible for a later split under this amendment UNTIL THE NAMED DESIGN LEFTOVER IS CLOSED'. The closed-name-list reading therefore exists only in the COORD entry's compressed one-paragraph Decision, which D-087 produced when it 'unioned the eligible/ineligible row-name sentence into the kept Decision'. Two consequences follow. (a) The entry supersedes something D-056's adopted subject never said, while simultaneously listing D-056's Eligibility gates under 'Stands, unchanged' — the gates and the superseded 'definition' are the same clause of the same subject, so the entry both preserves and supersedes one artifact without distinguishing them. (b) The draft names only the eligible sentence and gives the ineligible sentence no standing at all, yet its own Ineligible table asserts the mechanism 'A later own cycle may move one row only by closing the named leftover so that the five gates then hold.' Read against the COORD paragraph alone — the text every later entry actually cites, including D-131 — 'DR-103/104/105/114/118 and the twelve no-contract rows remain ineligible' is flat and unqualified, so that mechanism has no recorded basis and the first later cycle that moves DR-103 or DR-117 off it will be moving a D-056 by-name holding with no named supersession. That is the DR-204 provenance defect in its exact recorded form.
mustFix.whyBlocking: The entry's Why-clause is the load-bearing justification for a scoped successor to an adopted decision, and it is wrong at the pinned bytes. An adopted D-133 would leave the corpus with a supersession pointed at the wrong artifact, a subject whose already-correct property statement is stranded, and a by-name ineligible sentence whose lifting mechanism is asserted in a successor but grounded nowhere. This cycle's own attack list names both halves — 'silently moves a named D-056 ineligibility' and 'supersession is unnamed or over-broad'.
mustFix.repair: Rewrite 'Why this entry exists' and 'What is superseded' to say what is measurably true: D-056's pinned turn-2 subject already states eligibility as a property, labels its four-row table 'Motivating later candidates' and its ineligible table 'named, not exhaustive ... until the named design leftover is closed'; the closed-list reading arises only in the COORD entry's compressed Decision paragraph as unioned by D-087. Scope the supersession to that COORD paragraph's two name-list sentences — BOTH of them, named — holding each as a dated measurement rather than a definition, with the subject's five gates governing. Then keep the rest of the entry as drafted: the tables, the row-by-row instruction, the refusal of an admit-limb and the Stands list all survive this correction unchanged, and the entry becomes narrower and better grounded, not weaker.

coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 1 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX, with 3 non-blocking advisories. Twenty-eight attacks run, three landed on two distinct defects. Custody is intact at both ends: subject e548bd46 at 0444, HEAD never left d3efe3c, and COORD, file 08 and file 12 all held their pins with the governing tree clean. All five measured-inputs rows reproduce exactly. The entry's purpose is sound and D-132 clause 2 authorizes precisely it; most of the draft is strong, and its 30-row two-table measurement is the best thing in it — 4 eligible + 5 named ineligible + 12 no-contract + 9 deferral covers DR-101..DR-130 exactly once each, the twelve match D-056's own enumeration, and the 4-of-30 snapshot claim is current. The blocking defect is that the entry's justification does not survive its own predecessor's pinned subject. D-056's adopted turn-2 subject at dfb0c2af already states eligibility as a property applied 'at the moment of that later cycle', already labels its four-row table 'Motivating later candidates', and already heads its ineligible table 'named, not exhaustive ... until the named design leftover is closed'. The closed-name-list reading the draft supersedes exists only in the COORD entry's compressed Decision paragraph, produced by D-087's union — and the draft names only the eligible half of that paragraph, leaving the ineligible half with no stated standing while asserting a mechanism that lifts it. As drafted the entry would supersede something its predecessor never said, strand the subject's already-correct property statement, and hand the first later cycle that moves DR-103 or DR-117 an unnamed supersession of a by-name D-056 holding. The repair is narrow: correct the Why-clause to the pinned bytes and scope the supersession to the COORD paragraph's two name-list sentences, both named, as dated measurements rather than definitions. The SHOULD-FIX is a false universal: the twelve-row cell claims three properties hold for each recording; the Class-A conjunct holds for all twelve and carries the conclusion, but 'binds NOTHING' is absent from four and 'leftover-design' from eight. I record that my own earlier attack on the 'Stands, unchanged' enumeration failed — that text is verbatim in D-056's pinned subject, and ATK-24 is logged refuted.
